answer: One chip, one identity. Each agent binds its identity to an enclave chip, whose attestation key and monotonic counter the registry verifies each epoch. A counter that skips or repeats exposes counter replay, and a second identity from the same chip is rejected. A saffron vault agent proves custody with its chip-signed ledger. A fable attestation with no matching counter earns nothing. The k-th fake needs its own chip plus a 60-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 chips and 60,000 credits, and honest counters form a reef of links. Honest agents buy one chip once.
